\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{موافقت} \fa{کردن} (movâfeqat kardan)}{موافقت کردن (movâfeqat kardan)}]{\fa{موافقت} \fa{کردن} (movâfeqat kardan) — to agree, to consent}

\label{lesson:FA-C361-movafeqat-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to believe, then the Persian for a theory.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{موافقت} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{موافقت} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{movâfeqat kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to agree, to consent\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مدیر} \fa{با} \fa{پیشنهاد} \fa{ما} \fa{موافقت} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{modir bâ pishnahâd-e mâ movâfeqat kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The manager agreed to our proposal.
\end{quote}

Takes \emph{bâ}: \emph{bâ chizi movâfeqat kardan}. \emph{Movâfeqat} \textquotedblleft{}agreement\textquotedblright{} + \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} (present stem \emph{kon-}). Compare \emph{movâfeq budan}, to agree in opinion.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{موافقت}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{muwāfaqa} \textquotedblleft{}agreement, consent\textquotedblright{}, from the same Arabic family as \emph{movâfeq} \textquotedblleft{}agreeing\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is the inherited Persian verb.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{movâfeqat kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{movâfeqat kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{movâfeqat kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to believe, then the Persian for a theory, then say \emph{movâfeqat kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{موافقت} \fa{کردن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To agree, to consent\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مخالفت} \fa{کردن} (mokhâlefat kardan)}{مخالفت کردن (mokhâlefat kardan)}]{\fa{مخالفت} \fa{کردن} (mokhâlefat kardan) — to oppose, to object to}

\label{lesson:FA-C361-mokhalefat-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a theory, then the Persian for to agree.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مخالفت} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{مخالفت} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{mokhâlefat kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to oppose, to object to\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پدرم} \fa{با} \fa{سفر} \fa{من} \fa{مخالفت} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pedaram bâ safar-e man mokhâlefat kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father opposed my trip.
\end{quote}

Takes \emph{bâ}: \emph{bâ chizi mokhâlefat kardan}. \emph{Mokhâlefat} \textquotedblleft{}opposition\textquotedblright{} + \emph{kardan} (stem \emph{kon-}).

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{مخالفت}} is derived from \emph{mokhâlef} \textquotedblleft{}opposed, contrary\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), a word of Arabic origin, usually traced to Arabic \emph{mukhālafa} \textquotedblleft{}opposition\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{mokhâlefat kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a theory, then the Persian for to agree, then say \emph{mokhâlefat kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مخالف} (mokhâlef)}{مخالف (mokhâlef)}]{\fa{مخالف} (mokhâlef) — opposed, against; an opponent}

\label{lesson:FA-C361-mokhalef}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to agree, then the Persian for to oppose.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مخالف}}
\textbf{\fa{مخالف}} (\emph{mokhâlef}) — \textquotedblleft{}opposed, against; an opponent\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بیشتر} \fa{مردم} \fa{با} \fa{این} \fa{طرح} \fa{مخالف} \fa{هستند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bishtar-e mardom bâ in tarh mokhâlef hastand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Most people are against this plan.
\end{quote}

\emph{Bâ chizi mokhâlef budan} — to be against something. The opposite is \emph{movâfeq}. As a noun, an opponent: plural \emph{mokhâlefân}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{مخالف}} \textquotedblleft{}contrary, opposed\textquotedblright{} is in EtymDB; it is usually traced to Arabic \emph{mukhālif} \textquotedblleft{}opposing, going against\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mokhâlef}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to agree, then the Persian for to oppose, then say \emph{mokhâlef} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{باور} \fa{داشتن} (bâvar dâshtan)}{باور داشتن (bâvar dâshtan)}]{\fa{باور} \fa{داشتن} (bâvar dâshtan) — to believe in, to have faith in}

\label{lesson:FA-C361-bavar-dashtan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to oppose, then the Persian for opposed.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{باور} \fa{داشتن}}
\textbf{\fa{باور} \fa{داشتن}} (\emph{bâvar dâshtan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to believe in, to have faith in\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{به} \fa{خودش} \fa{باور} \fa{دارد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u be khodash bâvar dârad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She believes in herself.
\end{quote}

\emph{Bâvar} \textquotedblleft{}belief\textquotedblright{} + \emph{dâshtan} \textquotedblleft{}to have\textquotedblright{} (present stem \emph{dâr-}). Takes \emph{be}: \emph{be chizi bâvar dâshtan}. Compare \emph{bâvar kardan}, to believe a statement.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{باور} \fa{داشتن}} is native Persian, built from \emph{bâvar} \textquotedblleft{}belief\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{wābar}, and \emph{dâshtan} \textquotedblleft{}to have\textquotedblright{}, the inherited verb.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bâvar dâshtan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{bâvar dâshtan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to oppose, then the Persian for opposed, then say \emph{bâvar dâshtan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{شک} \fa{داشتن} (shak dâshtan)}{شک داشتن (shak dâshtan)}]{\fa{شک} \fa{داشتن} (shak dâshtan) — to doubt, to be unsure}

\label{lesson:FA-C361-shak-dashtan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for opposed, then the Persian for to believe in.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{شک} \fa{داشتن}}
\textbf{\fa{شک} \fa{داشتن}} (\emph{shak dâshtan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to doubt, to be unsure\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{من} \fa{در} \fa{درستی} \fa{این} \fa{خبر} \fa{شک} \fa{دارم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{man dar dorosti-ye in khabar shak dâram.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I doubt that this news is true.
\end{quote}

\emph{Shak} \textquotedblleft{}doubt\textquotedblright{} + \emph{dâshtan} (stem \emph{dâr-}). Takes \emph{dar} or \emph{be}: \emph{dar chizi shak dâshtan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{شک}} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{shakk} \textquotedblleft{}doubt\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB); \emph{dâshtan} \textquotedblleft{}to have\textquotedblright{} is the inherited Persian verb, so the phrase is literally to have a doubt.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{shak dâshtan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for opposed, then the Persian for to believe in, then say \emph{shak dâshtan} again
\end{itemize}
